response.description: Built and tested on court judgment recitals only, not on the merits of any case. No lawyer has used this on a live matter. The complaint window, holidays and the Limitation Act counting rules are not computed: they are referred to a lawyer.

conventions.A: first day excluded, last day included (default)
conventions.rule: both are computed; when the answer differs the step answers REFER with both counts

steps.title: presented to the bank within six months of the date drawn, or within the cheque's validity
steps.result: The dates you entered fall inside the stated period (both counts agree: months from the date drawn)

A.convention: first day excluded, last day included

notes: The cheque validity of 3 months was entered by you; it is not in the section. A validity shorter than six months ends the period earlier; a longer one does not extend it past six months

steps.title: notice in writing to the drawer within thirty days of receiving the bank's information of the return
steps.result: The dates you entered fall inside the stated period (both counts agree: days from the information)

A.convention: first day excluded, last day included

steps.title: the drawer's fifteen days to pay run from receiving the notice
steps.result: The fifteen days run to 2013-03-12 (first day excluded) or 2013-03-11 (first day included); whether the drawer paid is not assessed here

A.convention: first day excluded, last day included

steps.title: the complaint window

refer.text: The complaint window comes from s.142, which is not held: it is not computed here; a lawyer sets it. Nothing on this list says whether a complaint is in time

steps.result: REFER: The complaint window comes from s.142, which is not held: it is not computed here; a lawyer sets it. Nothing on this list says whether a complaint is in time.

not_assessed: Whether the underlying debt is legally enforceable, or still recoverable in time
Whether the cheque was drawn for the discharge of a debt or other liability (s.138 requires it)
The reason the bank gave for returning the cheque (s.138 names insufficiency of funds, or an amount over the arrangement with the bank)
Whether the notice demands more than is due
How the notice was served and whether it was received
Notices to a company and its directors (s.141)
The standing of the payee or holder
notes: Holiday check not performed: if a last day was a court holiday, the next working day may apply (a lawyer sets the rule)
